title: Finite presentation under finite finitely presented direct image
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A morphism is finite if representable and finite on all scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Local finite presentation is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation additionally requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, meaning a quasi-compact relative diagonal. Use modules on the small etale structure sheaves, quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback and module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it admits an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite, and of finite type if etale locally finitely generated. Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite and of finite presentation, and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Then $f_*M$ is quasi-coherent and $M$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_X$ if and only if $f_*M$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_Y$. No Noetherian, flatness, or absolute quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0610 (lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module); quasi-coherence of the affine direct image as in spaces-morphisms.tex, lemma-pushforward.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $q:V\to Y$ from a scheme, and set $U=X\times_YV$, with $p:U\to X$ and $\psi:U\to V$. Representability of the finite map $f$ makes $U$ a scheme, and the fibre-product covering lemma makes $p$ surjective etale. By the scheme-test meaning of finite, $\psi$ is finite. Apply the chart criterion for local finite presentation to $V\to Y$ and the identity atlas of $X\times_YV=U$: $\psi$ is locally of finite presentation. Since a finite scheme map is affine, affine permanence makes $\psi$ quasi-compact and separated, as required for the scheme direct-image comparison below. Restricting local presentations shows that $M_U=M|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0610, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, first two sentences of the proof; Tag 0410, spaces-morphisms.tex lemma-finite-presentation-local.

proof.text: Every affine scheme test of $f$ is a finite scheme morphism with affine target, hence has affine source. Thus $f$ is an affine morphism of algebraic spaces. The quasi-coherence clause of the affine direct-image theorem gives that $f_*M$ is quasi-coherent. The etale pushforward restriction comparison gives the canonical isomorphism $G=(f_*M)|_{V_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq\psi_{\mathrm{et},*}M_U$ of $\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{et}}$-modules. Its sections on an etale $W\to V$ are the identity on the compatible sections of $M$ over $X\times_Y W=U\times_VW$; thus it compares the specified module direct images, including their scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, quasi-coherence clause; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX, lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules, degree zero; the displayed restriction identity in the proof of Tag 0610.

proof.text: Under the scheme Zariski-small-etale quasi-coherent equivalence, write $M_U\simeq A_U(F)$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F$ on $U$. Because $\psi$ is quasi-compact and separated, the same equivalence identifies $\psi_{\mathrm{et},*}M_U$ with $A_V(\psi_*F)$, where $\psi_*F$ is the Zariski direct image and is quasi-coherent. The finiteness comparison says $M_U$ is finitely presented exactly when $F$ is, and $A_V(\psi_*F)$ is finitely presented exactly when $\psi_*F$ is. The scheme finite-pushforward preservation lemma gives $F$ finitely presented $\Rightarrow\psi_*F$ finitely presented; the reflection lemma gives the reverse implication. Both apply because $\psi$ is finite and locally of finite presentation and $F$ is quasi-coherent. Consequently $M_U$ is finitely presented if and only if $G$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent, small-etale part; Tag 03LC, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial, part (3); Tag 05VG, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties; Tag 05B4, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module.

proof.text: Finite presentation in the item means etale locally the cokernel of a map between finite free modules. It is therefore equivalent to finite presentation after restriction to the atlas $p:U\to X$: one direction restricts the local exact presentations on localized sites, and the other composes their covering families with $p$. Covers pull back and compose by the cited covering calculus, and etale restriction identifies the structure sheaves and is restriction to these localized sites. The same argument applies to $q:V\to Y$. Hence $M$ is finitely presented $\Leftrightarrow M_U$ is finitely presented $\Leftrightarrow G$ is finitely presented $\Leftrightarrow f_*M$ is finitely presented. Together with step 2 this proves both assertions. All covers are allowed to be infinite; the argument imposes no absolute quasi-compactness or Noetherian or flatness hypothesis.
